body:
## Summary
This PR addresses critical performance bottlenecks identified in issue #14196 where the pharmacy fast retail sale page was experiencing slow loading times due to excessive getter method calls and inefficient rendering patterns.

### Performance Issues Resolved
- **Excessive getter calls**: `getPreBill()` called 25+ times, `getPatient()` called 27+ times during page load
- **Slow reset operations**: `resetAll()` method taking 269ms with unnecessary operations
- **Property chain navigation overhead**: Repeated JSF expression evaluation

### Key Optimizations Implemented

#### 🚀 **1. Request-Scoped Caching (Java Controller)**
- Added caching fields: `cachedPreBill`, `cachedPatient` with validity flags
- Enhanced `getPreBill()` and `getPatient()` methods with request-scoped caching
- Proper cache invalidation in setters and data clearing methods
- Centralized cache management via `invalidateAllCaches()` method

#### 🚀 **2. XHTML Property Chain Optimization**
- Added `c:set` tags to cache frequently accessed property chains
- Cached variables: `cachedController`, `cachedPreBill`, `cachedPatient`, `cachedBillItem`, `cachedPaymentMethodData`
- Reduced JSF expression evaluation overhead throughout the page

#### 🚀 **3. resetAll() Method Performance**
- Conditional user stock retirement (only when containers exist)
- Centralized cache invalidation after reset operations
- Eliminated unnecessary database operations during page navigation

#### 🚀 **4. Lazy Initialization Improvements**
- Stock search optimization: Return empty list for queries < 3 characters
- Allergy list optimization: Only load when patient is valid (`patient.getId() \!= null`)
- Settlement validation: Check prerequisites before expensive operations

### Expected Performance Impact
- **50-70% reduction** in page load time
- **Elimination** of excessive getter call bottleneck
- **Faster** reset operations and navigation
- **Improved** user experience and page responsiveness

### Testing Results
✅ **User Confirmation**: "its working perfectly" - Performance improvements validated in testing environment

### Files Changed
- `PharmacyFastRetailSaleController.java` - Request-scoped caching and performance optimizations
- `pharmacy_fast_retail_sale.xhtml` - Property chain caching with c:set tags
- `LOCAL_ENV_NOTES.md` - Environment documentation for future debugging

## Test plan
- [x] Page load performance tested and confirmed improved
- [x] Excessive getter calls eliminated (verified in logs)
- [x] Reset operations faster and more efficient
- [x] All existing functionality preserved
- [x] No breaking changes to business logic

Closes #14196

body:
## 🎯 Overview

This PR implements a loading spinner for project images on the projects page to improve user experience when images are still loading. Previously, users would see blank space or broken-looking layouts while images loaded, which could make the page appear incomplete.

## 🚀 What's New

### Reusable ImageWithSpinner Component
Created a new reusable component (`src/components/ImageWithSpinner/index.tsx`) that:
- Shows a purple loading spinner while images are loading
- Smoothly transitions to the actual image once loaded (0.3s fade-in)
- Handles error states gracefully with fallback messaging
- Maintains accessibility with proper ARIA labels
- Is fully responsive and works with existing Chakra UI styling

### Key Features
- **Loading States**: Visual spinner indication during image loading
- **Smooth Transitions**: Clean fade-in effect when images load
- **Error Handling**: Displays "Failed to load image" message for broken images
- **Accessibility**: Proper alt text and ARIA labels for screen readers
- **Responsive Design**: Maintains existing layout and styling
- **Configurable**: Customizable spinner size and color

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

The component uses React hooks for state management:
```typescript
const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true)
const [hasError, setHasError] = useState(false)
```

And leverages native image events:
```typescript
const handleLoad = () => setIsLoading(false)
const handleError = () => { setIsLoading(false); setHasError(true) }
```

## 📸 Visual Results

**Before**: Images would appear instantly or show blank space while loading
**After**: Shows loading spinner, then smooth transition to loaded image

![Projects page with loading spinner implementation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0a8f3e5-1195-4adb-af13-b566d4ee83ce)

The hover effects are fully preserved:

![Hover effects still working correctly](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6364c1f7-4f52-4cdd-aa1a-d6f3db179b02)

## 🔄 Changes Made

1. **Created** `src/components/ImageWithSpinner/index.tsx` - New reusable component with loading states
2. **Updated** `src/pages/projects/index.tsx` - Replaced direct Image usage with ImageWithSpinner
3. **Fixed** hydration error by removing nested anchor tags (replaced NextLink + Link with simple anchor)

## ✅ Testing

- ✅ Build passes successfully
- ✅ Linting passes (no new warnings)
- ✅ All existing functionality preserved (hover effects, navigation)
- ✅ Loading states work correctly
- ✅ Error handling works for broken images
- ✅ Responsive design maintained
- ✅ Accessibility improvements (better alt text)

## 🎯 Acceptance Criteria Met

- ✅ Loading spinner appears as placeholder while images load
- ✅ Smooth transition from spinner to loaded image
- ✅ Reusable component for all project images
- ✅ Maintains accessibility and responsiveness
- ✅ Handles error states gracefully

Resolves #1

body: I came across this while working on a custom Ant task. I saw what I think is the ResourceCollection stream() method eagerly loading elements when creating a stream. Not sure if that was intentional or not. If it is, feel free to close the PR.  If not, I've created this to update it to use the StreamSupport factory method and a spliterator. I think this is how the JDK Collection creates the stream. This will make using things like findFirst a bit faster as it won't have to load every element to find the first.

author: shamoo53
body:
This pull request adds a new system logs module to the application. The goal of this module is to track and store important events that happen across the system, such as failed login attempts, successful clock-ins, and configuration changes.

The system logs module is built as a fully independent feature, meaning it does not depend on any other service or domain. It can be plugged into the existing system without introducing side effects or tight coupling. All log entries are stored in a dedicated database table called "system_logs". Each log entry contains three key pieces of information: the type of event (for example, "LOGIN_FAILED"), a detailed message describing the event, and a timestamp that is automatically recorded when the log is created.

In addition to recording logs, the module also provides the ability to search through them. Logs can be filtered based on the type of event, a specific time range, and they support pagination using offset and limit. This makes it easier for administrators or developers to retrieve and review specific types of system activity efficiently.

The service logic is covered by unit tests using Jest. These tests check the creation of logs and the filtering functionality to ensure everything works correctly. The database interaction is mocked to isolate the logic from external dependencies.

This new feature improves the system’s observability and makes it easier to track what’s happening at any given time. It supports security monitoring, debugging, auditing, and future compliance needs. It also sets the foundation for future improvements like role-based access control for logs, integration with third-party monitoring platforms, and the ability to export or archive logs.

In summary, this pull request adds a foundational and reusable logging system that increases transparency and reliability across the application.

author: fan-ziqi
body:
## 👀 Overview

I'm excited to announce the release of **robot_lab 2.2.0**! This version supports **IsaacLab2.2.0** and **IsaacSim5.0.0**, uses urdf/xacro/mjcf instead of USD, and support for more robot models. Here are the main updates:

## 🔆 Highlighted Changes:

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/fan-ziqi/robot_lab/compare/v2.1...v2.2.0

1. Compatibility Updates

  - Supported [IsaacLab-2.2.0](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/releases/tag/v2.2.0) and [IsaacSim-5.0.0](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacSim).
  - Python version has been updated to 3.11 from 3.10.
  - PyTorch version is updated to torch 2.7.0+cu128, which will include Blackwell support.


2. Use urdf/xacro/mjcf instead of USD

    This version supports direct import of URDF, XACRO, and MJCF robot models without requiring pre-conversion to USD format.

    ```python
    from robot_lab.assets.utils.usd_converter import (  # noqa: F401
        mjcf_to_usd,
        spawn_from_lazy_usd,
        urdf_to_usd,
        xacro_to_usd,
    )
    
    YOUR_ROBOT_CFG = ArticulationCfg(
        spawn=sim_utils.UsdFileCfg(
            # for urdf
            func=spawn_from_lazy_usd,
            usd_path=urdf_to_usd(
                file_path=f"{ISAACLAB_ASSETS_DATA_DIR}/Robots/your_robot/your_robot.urdf",
                merge_joints=True,
                fix_base=False,
            ),
            # for xacro
            func=spawn_from_lazy_usd,
            usd_path=xacro_to_usd(
                file_path=f"{ISAACLAB_ASSETS_DATA_DIR}/Robots/your_robot/your_robot.xacro",
                merge_joints=True,
                fix_base=False,
            ),
            # for mjcf
            func=spawn_from_lazy_usd,
            usd_path=mjcf_to_usd(
                file_path=f"{ISAACLAB_ASSETS_DATA_DIR}/Robots/your_robot/your_robot.xml",
                import_sites=True,
                fix_base=False,
            ),
            # ... other configuration parameters ...
        ),
        # ... other configuration parameters ...
    )
    ```

3. New Robot Supports

    Added **Deeprobotics Lite3**, **Deeprobotics X30**, **Deeprobotics M20**, **Booster T1**, **RobotEra Xbot** , **Openloong Loong** , **DDTRobot Tita** robots.

4. Add Unitree-G1 AMP SKRL direct-based enviroment

5. Tasks have been reworked and restructured. Notably, the following paths were updated: 
- `robot_lab.tasks.locomotion` --> `robot_lab.tasks.manager_based.locomotion`

## ✈️ Roadmap

- Add more **robot models** and **training code** — community contributions are welcome!

## 🤗 Support & Contribution

If you enjoy this project, please **Star** it! It’s the motivation behind my continuous updates. If you have any questions, suggestions, or want to contribute, feel free to submit **issues** or **pull requests**.

--- 🔧 This PR marks login workflows as auto-generated to prevent them from cluttering the workflow history UI. The change adds a status parameter to automatically created login workflows, making them invisible in the standard workflow listing while maintaining their functionality.
🔍 Detailed Analysis ### Key Changes - **Workflow Status Enhancement**: Added `WorkflowStatus` import to support the new auto-generated status classification - **Login Workflow Marking**: Modified the login workflow creation to include `status=WorkflowStatus.auto_generated` parameter - **UI/UX Improvement**: Prevents automatically generated login workflows from appearing in user-facing workflow history ### Technical Implementation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant API as Login API participant WF as Workflow Service participant UI as Workflow History UI User->>API: Request login workflow API->>WF: Create workflow with status=auto_generated WF->>WF: Process login workflow Note over UI: Auto-generated workflows filtered out UI->>User: Shows only user-created workflows ``` ### Impact - **Cleaner User Experience**: Users will no longer see system-generated login workflows in their workflow history - **Improved Organization**: Separates user-initiated workflows from system-generated ones for better workflow management - **Backward Compatibility**: Existing functionality remains unchanged, only adds metadata to distinguish workflow types
_Created with [Palmier](https://www.palmier.io)_ ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Sets `status=WorkflowStatus.auto_generated` in `login()` in `run_blocks.py` to mark workflows as auto-generated. > > - **Behavior**: > - Sets `status=WorkflowStatus.auto_generated` in `login()` in `run_blocks.py` to mark workflows as auto-generated. > - **Imports**: > - Adds `WorkflowStatus` to imports in `run_blocks.py`. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=Skyvern-AI%2Fskyvern&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 1ee9c15949a1f3649a33ab602426a2cec4904904.
